title: Slow-Cooked Beef Rendang with Toasted Coconut
summary: A rich, slow-braised beef curry deeply flavoured with toasted coconut, citrus leaves and a fragrant chilli paste, simmered until dark, thick and glossy.
equipment: wok or wide heavy pan with lid

ingredients.item: dried red chillies, about 7 cm long
lemongrass stalks, tender lower part, sliced
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Soak 8 dried red chillies in cold water for 1 h until soft, then drain and chop.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blitz the chillies with 120 g shallots, 2 lemongrass stalks, 6 garlic cloves and the chopped ginger with 80 ml water to a smooth paste.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat 5 tbsp oil in a wok until very hot, add the paste and fry for 1-2 min until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add 700 g beef, 240 ml coconut milk and 280 ml water, bring to the boil, cover and simmer gently for 30 min.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Stir in 6 lime leaves, 60 ml tamarind liquid, 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast 40 g desiccated coconut in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 min until light golden, then stir into the beef.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on low until the beef is very tender, 60-75 min, stirring occasionally and adding a splash of water if it catches.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: Uncover and cook, stirring often, until the sauce is thick and dark and the oil separates, 15-20 min.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Remove the lime leaves and serve hot with steamed rice.

tips: Browning the spice paste properly before adding the beef is what gives the dish its deep flavour, so don't rush this step.
Keep the heat low once the beef goes in, lifting the lid now and then and topping up with a splash of water if the sauce catches.
The dish is ready when the sauce has reduced right down and a thin layer of oil separates on top.
storage: Once cooled, cover and keep in the fridge for a few days, or freeze in portions, reheating gently on the hob until piping hot throughout. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
